# Pondhawk.Rules

> A standalone .NET forward-chaining rule engine by Pond Hawk Technologies with type-based fact matching, a fluent rule/validation API, and weighted decision scoring — plus an EF Core SaveChanges validation adapter. Two packages, both target net8.0, no dependency on other Pondhawk packages.

## Packages

### Pondhawk.Rules — rule engine

Install: `dotnet add package Pondhawk.Rules`

**Key types:**
- `RuleSet` (`Pondhawk.Rules.Factory`) — runtime rule/validation creation: `.AddRule<T>(name)`, `.AddValidation<T>(name)`, `.Evaluate(facts)`, `.TryValidate(fact, out violations)`, `.Decide(fact)`
- `Rule<TFact>` — `.When(pred).And(pred).Then(action)`; scoring `.FireAffirm(weight)` / `.FireVeto(weight)` (also `.ThenAffirm` / `.ThenVeto`)
- `ValidationRule<TFact>` — `.Assert<T>(expr).Required()...` (validators run at very high salience)
- `RuleBuilder<TFact>` — class-based rule sets (subclass; define rules in the constructor via `Rule()`)
- `ValidationBuilder<TFact>` — class-based validations
- `IRuleSet` — evaluate / validate / decide
- `EvaluationResults` — events, `Score`, violations, timing, fired-rule stats
- DI: `services.UseRules(assembly)` (also `services.AddRules(...)`) — discovers builders from assemblies

**Rule fluent API:**
```csharp
var ruleSet = new RuleSet();
ruleSet.AddRule<Order>("high-value")
    .When(o => o.Total > 1000)
    .And(o => o.Status == "Pending")
    .Then(o => o.RequiresApproval = true);

var results = ruleSet.Evaluate(order);   // results.TotalFired, results.Events, results.Score
```
Rules match across up to 4 fact types. Per-fact predicate overloads enable C# pattern matching:
```csharp
ruleSet.AddRule<Person, Order>("gold-discount")
    .When((Func<Person, bool>)(p => p.Tier is "Gold" or "Platinum"))
    .And((Func<Order, bool>)(o => o.Total is > 200 and < 10_000))
    .Then((p, o) => o.DiscountPct = 0.10m);
```

**Validation:**
```csharp
ruleSet.AddValidation<Person>("name").Assert(p => p.Name).Required();
ruleSet.AddValidation<Person>("email").Assert(p => p.Email).Required().IsEmail();
bool ok = ruleSet.TryValidate(person, out var violations);
```

**Scoring / decisions:** `.FireAffirm(w)` / `.FireVeto(w)` accumulate into `Score`; `ruleSet.Decide(fact)` returns bool.
**Controls:** salience (priority), mutex (only the first matching rule in a group fires), fire-once, inception/expiration.
**Forward chaining:** modifying/inserting/retracting facts re-triggers evaluation.
**Authoring guidelines:** avoid `||` in a condition — write one rule per OR branch (atomic, individually traceable); prefer `.And()` chains over `&&`.

### Pondhawk.Rules.EFCore — EF Core SaveChanges validation

Install: `dotnet add package Pondhawk.Rules.EFCore`
```csharp
var options = new DbContextOptionsBuilder<AppContext>()
    .UseSqlServer(connectionString)
    .AddRuleValidation(ruleSet)
    .Options;
```
`RuleValidationInterceptor : SaveChangesInterceptor` validates all `Added`/`Modified` entities through `IRuleSet.Validate()` before the save reaches the database; throws `EntityValidationException` (structured violations) on failure. Requires EF Core 5.0+ (the release that introduced SaveChanges interception).

## Technical details
- Both packages target `net8.0`
- XML documentation ships inside the NuGet packages (100% public-API coverage; consumers get IntelliSense)
- MIT licensed; extracted from the pondhawktech/tools monorepo (now pondhawk-utilities)
